records.notes:
SIX, exactly — counted twice in IMG_3508 and IMG_3509 and identical both times. On a low wooden dock: PROTOCOL.md 5b man_made_perch, NOTED and not counted.

PHENOLOGY: one bird is a drake in FULL BREEDING PLUMAGE — glossy green head, chestnut breast, clean grey flanks. Every earlier mallard in the record from July onward reads "female or eclipse". This is the first unambiguous breeding-plumage drake since March, so the eclipse moult is finishing by late September.

Also the second-best hard-mark check in the log after the 09-17 dock cormorant, and for the same reason: birds standing on bare decking put their legs in plain view, which water never does.

records.notes: Two adults clearly resolved in IMG_3539; IMG_3540 adds a third white shape much further east that is probably a third swan but is not resolvable, hence the range. No cygnets anywhere in this walk — the first date since June with adults present and no brood in frame. Not evidence of loss: this is the far west end and the family ranges widely.
